## October 10: One Swing, One Hit

You know, after covering playoff baseball for more years than I care to admit, there's something satisfying about a clean 1-0 day. No drama, no second-guessing—just a straightforward call on the Guardians that landed exactly where we expected. Sometimes the best predictions are the ones that feel inevitable from the first pitch.

## The Guardians Call: Why It Worked

This wasn't about getting cute with the numbers. Cleveland at home in October? I've seen this movie before. The model liked them at 53%, which in playoff baseball might as well be a neon sign. When you're getting value on a home team with postseason experience, you take it and don't look back.

The Sox came in swinging, sure, but Progressive Field in October has a way of tilting things. Home crowd, familiar surroundings, and that Guardians pitching staff doing what it does best. Textbook.

## Looking Ahead: October 11's Main Event

Now here's where it gets interesting. The model is practically screaming at us to back Milwaukee tomorrow, and with good reason. We're looking at a 61% confidence level on the Brewers—that's not a whisper, that's a statement.

## The Pitching Matchup: Experience vs. Potential

Tarik Skubal coming to town with the Dodgers? Yeah, that's a problem for most teams. The guy's got postseason pedigree and that nasty slider that makes hitters look silly. But here's the thing—Jacob Misiorowski at American Family Field is a different animal.

I've watched enough young arms flame out in big moments to be skeptical, but Misiorowski isn't your typical youngster. The kid's got plus stuff, and more importantly, he's got that short memory you need in October. The Brewers wouldn't be rolling him out there if they didn't trust him in this spot.

## Why Milwaukee at 61%?

Let me break down what the model sees, because it aligns with what my gut's been telling me:

**Home field advantage in October**: Milwaukee's crowd doesn't mess around. They've been waiting for this.

**The Dodgers' October road struggles**: I've covered enough of these series to know LA plays differently away from Chavez Ravine when the stakes are highest.

**Bullpen depth**: Milwaukee's got fresh arms. That matters in Game 2 situations.

This isn't a fadeaway from the Dodgers—it's recognition that 61% on a home underdog with the right matchup is exactly where you want to be. The value is screaming at us.

## The Bottom Line

We went 1-0 yesterday by trusting the process and not overthinking it. Tomorrow, the model's giving us an even stronger signal with Milwaukee. In my experience, when you get a 61% confidence level on a home team in October, you don't fade it—you ride it.

Skubal's good. Real good. But baseball in October has a way of humbling even the best arms when they're on the road. I'll take Misiorowski, the Milwaukee crowd, and that 61% confidence all day long.

Let's make it 2-0.
